psychedelic: RE104 (4-OH-DiPT glutarate prodrug), RE109 (psilocin glutarate prodrug), 4-OH-DiPT

age.evidence: Adult male Wistar rats 8-10 weeks of age

sex.evidence: Antidepressant-like effects were evaluated using a modified FST in Wistar rats (exclusively males to limit potential variability)

dosing.evidence: single SC intraperitoneal injection dose of vehicle ... 1 mg/kg RE104 ... IV or SC administration of 2 mg/kg RE104
dose of 4-OH-DiPT was adjusted to 1.39 mg/kg to match the molar dose (5.34 µmol/kg) of RE104

assays.assay_description: Rats observed for head twitches (wet dog shakes) after IV or SC administration of RE104 (2 mg/kg) or 4-OH-DiPT (1.39 mg/kg). HTRs manually counted in 10 min intervals up to 2 h post-dose and again at 3, 3.5, and 4 h.

application_type.evidence: IV and SC administration of 2 mg/kg RE104 and 1.39 mg/kg 4-OH-DiPT

setup_restrain.evidence: HTRs were manually counted... observing rats for automatisms

time_to_assay.evidence: HTRs were manually counted using 10 min intervals up to 2 h after dosing and again at 3, 3.5, and 4 h after dosing

outcomes.summary: RE104 (2 mg/kg) and 4-OH-DiPT (1.39 mg/kg) induced head-twitch responses that peaked immediately after IV administration and within 1 h after SC administration, then declined over the 4 h observation period. Mean HTR values correlated with plasma 4-OH-DiPT concentrations (r² = 0.7019).
outcomes.statistics: r² = 0.7019 (correlation between HTR and plasma 4-OH-DiPT concentration)
outcomes.evidence: HTR peaked immediately after IV administration of 2 mg/kg RE104 and 1.39 mg/kg 4-OH-DiPT and declined over the 4 h observation period.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: mean number of HTRs counted over 10 min intervals... as a function of time

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric

E2_shelter.evidence: not reported; not part of HTR observation

E8_food_water.evidence: no food/water in observation chamber during recording

D1_continuity.evidence: HTRs counted continuously across 10 min bins from dosing through 4 h on the dosing day

D2_session_duration.evidence: observation extended up to 4 h after dosing

D3_recording_days.evidence: single day of observation after dosing

assays.assay_description: Modified FST in male Wistar rats. 15 min pre-test exposure 24 h before, then 5 min test sessions in a 20 × 45 cm glass cylinder (35 cm of 25°C water) on days 7, 14, and 28 post-dose. Immobility, swimming, and climbing times scored by blinded observer from video.

application_type.evidence: single SC intraperitoneal injection dose of vehicle, 1 mg/kg RE104, an equivalent dose of RE109 (1 mg/kg), or ketamine (5 mg/kg, IP, single dose)

setup_habituation.evidence: Each rat was placed in a water-filled cylinder (20 cm in diameter and 45 cm in height) for 15 min for initial exposure 24 h before the test

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were placed individually in the glass cylinder

food_restriction.evidence: standard FST apparatus (water-filled cylinder); no food accessible during the 5 min test

water_restriction.evidence: no drinking water accessible in the water-filled cylinder during the test

time_to_assay.evidence: FST measurements were performed on days 7, 14, and 28

sample_size.evidence: n = 12 per treatment group; figure caption indicates n = 11-12

outcomes.summary: A single SC dose of RE104 (1 mg/kg) significantly reduced mean immobility time relative to vehicle on days 7, 14, and 28, with concomitant increases in swimming and climbing. RE109 (1 mg/kg) produced significant reductions in immobility on days 14 and 28.
outcomes.statistics: one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparison test or unpaired t-test; P < 0.001 for RE104 at day 7; P < 0.05 for RE104 on days 14 and 28 and RE109 on days 14 and 28
outcomes.evidence: A significant decrease in mean immobility time was observed for RE104 on days 7, 14, and 28, and for RE109 on days 14 and 28 (P < 0.05), demonstrating persistent effects with both compounds.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Immobility time, swimming time, and climbing time (in seconds) were measured

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: single total measured over the 5 min session

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric

B5_social.evidence: rats tested individually; not a social assay

B6_cognitive.evidence: FST does not require learning or memory

B7_automated_classification.evidence: measured from recorded videos by a blinded observer using a stopwatch

E1_environment_type.evidence: glass cylinder (20 cm diameter, 45 cm height) with water

E7_social_context.evidence: animals were placed individually in the glass cylinder

E8_food_water.evidence: no accessible food/water during 5 min test

D1_continuity.evidence: FST measurements were performed on days 7, 14, and 28

D4_baseline.evidence: 15 min pre-exposure was habituation only; no pre-drug behavioural data reported

D5_followup.evidence: FST on days 7, 14, 28 — all ≥24 h after dosing

judge_notes: Two behavioural assays retained: Head-Twitch Response (HTR/wet dog shakes) and Forced Swim Test. PK, receptor binding, prodrug cleavage, and metabolite profiling are non-behavioural and excluded.
B1 for HTR scored 0 (single measure: HTR count); B1 for FST scored 1 (immobility, swimming, climbing = 3 measures).
HTR D1 set to 'Single session' (score 0): the 4 h observation on the dosing day is a continuous within-session time course, not discrete sessions across days.
Strain noted as Wistar for FST (the only behavioural assay using strain explicitly named) and Sprague-Dawley for HTR/PK; reported both in 'strain' field.
Housing conditions and most experimental_conditions metadata for HTR set to not_reported (paper silent).
